system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
Which of these does NOT show a line of symmetry?

Figure, described in words:
Four shapes labeled A through D, each crossed by a straight line with arrowheads at both ends: A shows a vertically oriented block arrow pointing up, with a vertical line passing through the point of the arrow and the center of its base; B shows a horizontally elongated shape with zigzag top and bottom contours, with a horizontal line passing through the left and right tips; C shows a triangle with a horizontal line passing across it midway between the base and the top vertex; D shows a square with a diagonal line passing through the top-left and bottom-right corners.

A. [Image: An arrow pointing up with a vertical double-headed line through its center]
B. [Image: A horizontally elongated symmetric shape with zigzag edges and a horizontal double-headed line through its center]
C. [Image: A triangle with a horizontal double-headed line passing through it]
D. [Image: A square with a diagonal double-headed line connecting two opposite vertices]

answer.description: The letter of the option you choose for the question.
answer.title: Answer

llm_thinking:
I'm checking option A's vertical arrow symmetry, then examining option B's horizontally elongated zigzag shape to see if the top and bottom contours mirror each other across a horizontal axis.

For option C, a triangle with a horizontal line midway up doesn't reflect the shape onto itself—a real symmetry line would need to run from the apex to the midpoint of the base. Option D, the square's diagonal, clearly works as a symmetry line, so C is the one without a valid line of symmetry.
